instrumentChangesUnderTest: staged review with a named-gap repeat (proposed by the operator)
remediationCheck — the critic grades its own fix and states a confidence
scripts/verify-mutations.sh — a fixer's mutation claims replayed mechanically

remediationCheckCalibration.note: The headline result. Findings were reliably real; the FIXES attached to them were not. Every wrong one was caught by a separate agent re-deriving the fix, never by the suite.
remediationCheckCalibration.confidenceIsNotFindingQuality: Both xmpp findings marked `plausible` held up in FULL, while their remediations were wrong twice. The label tracks the critic's confidence in its fix, not in its finding — which is what it should do, but is the opposite of how it reads.
remediationCheckCalibration.wrongInSomeWay: at least 14 of 35 this round; 29 across rounds 9-15

failureModes.case: postgres: testsThatWouldFail said 'None found' and LISTED the three files it checked — none was the one file whose entire subject is what a reconnect leaves LISTENed, and 12 of whose 18 cells its own remediation breaks.

cases: redis: generate the expectations from the same array that drives the behaviour, so adding a bad value generates a row blessing it
sqlite: provoke read-only with chmod 0444, which does nothing when the suite runs as root
telegram: generalise the element generator to two calls that return no array and already pass explicit screens — a table with no reachable failing input

failureModes.mode: only the near side of a cross-system claim was traced
failureModes.case: zulip: asserted pydantic's StringConstraints calls Python str.strip(). It strips in Rust. All three reliesOn fields were traced against the plugin, never against the upstream the finding cites.

failureModes.mode: the fix converts an error into a silent wrong answer
failureModes.case: xmpp: folding a require() throw into `false` made fetchRecent on a never-connected plugin RESOLVE WITH AN EMPTY PAGE instead of rejecting.

failureModes.mode: the proposed property is false against correct code
cases: nats: a global cursor-monotonicity property, which read.ts deliberately violates when a cursor is judged restarted
conformance: fail any non-literal budget initializer, which makes a forwarded parameter a permanent red
discord: 'no comment says only ever' is false in eight packages, all correct risk prose

failureModes.mode: testsThatWouldFail: none because the fix is UNGRADED, not safe
failureModes.case: core F8: 'I applied findLast and ran the whole auth suite: 948 tests all pass' was TRUE — and the fix was completely ungraded, because the fixture seeded the owner with a minted code so the eviction pass could never reach it.
slack: proposed moving an invariant into bridge-core as a new test; core already owns it, better, and mutating the function reddens three core tests. The correct fix was pure deletion.

failureModes.mode: the remediation is insufficient rather than wrong
failureModes.case: telegram: 'carry ids served in this run plus ids holding records' still drops the mark on the load-repair path, because load() runs journalText from inside the constructor.

defectsFoundLargerThanFiled: matrix: the finding's own interleavings note claimed a partial collection 'is safe today and stays safe'. Measured false — at tail-noise depth limit-1 the reported cursor silently drops four messages, failing both before and after the narrow fix implied.
postgres: the teardown race was not only the pool — the listener socket has the identical shape in two more places, both dialling before publishing.
discord: the ratchet surfaced a sibling the finding never mentioned — a channel `type` destructure that crashes on null and accepts the string '0', silently unwiring a good channel forever.
nats: wss:// checked as a possible false positive and found not to be one, because connect.js wires only NodeTransport.

fixtureInfidelity.note: A recurring cause of invisibility: the fake is kinder than the server, so the guard cannot express the failure.
cases: postgres: FakePool.end settled without waiting for checked-out clients — it would have let disconnect() 'return clean' with a connection still out.
xmpp: FakeXmpp flagged EVERY last page complete, which would have stopped the new paging loop after one page and made an unpaged read look paged.
matrix: an absent timeline tip is illegitimate on real Synapse but legitimate in the fake, so the obvious fix would have broken every fresh-room subscribe for a fixture artefact.

newRatchetShapes: discord M2 and postgres M3 grade THE WRONG FIX rather than the defect — awaiting the handler, and the blind wake-all. Given that critics prescribe badly, a test that catches the attractive wrong answer is worth more than one catching only the original bug.
nats made the TRANSPORT the oracle instead of a table: a restored scheme allowlist fails even if the allowlist and a literal test agree with each other.
telegram graded what the fix BUYS (a flood cannot evict the chat) rather than how it is spelled, so the ratchet survives any change to the mark's format.
conformance compares two workflows against EACH OTHER rather than asserting either file's wording.
agentSelfCorrection: nats: refused to proceed when its findings file was missing, diagnosed the cause, and declined to fall back on stale round-5 findings — reasoning that inventing them would produce exactly the ungraded-fix failure the round exists to catch.

slack: told a wall-clock file was a known flake, declined to accept it; ran a HEAD control clean 3/3, established the file contains zero subscribe calls so its fix could not be the cause, and found the real cause was its own new tests raising contention.
xmpp: caught a tautology in its own test — counting redials could not discriminate, because destroying the socket is what makes start() reject, so the UNFIXED code's failure path passed the test.
core: watched its own anti-stub ratchet PASS under a stub that still increments the counter, and replaced it.
operatorErrors: Twice a mutation regex silently failed to match, so a suite passed against unmutated code and was nearly accepted as proof. This is what scripts/verify-mutations.sh now prevents by requiring exactly one match and asserting the file changed.

A false convergence: all 15 critics were blocked by a schema I had enlarged, agent() returned null rather than rejecting, and the runner mapped null to a clean result — so the round declared converged with 0 tokens spent and quiesced every target.

verification.behaviouralTestsInvertedReason: each encoded the defect as a requirement — an over-long topic matching on its bounded prefix, an OAuth store shedding the entry that must be protected, backoff expected to speed up above the ceiling
